summary: This React component provides a button that copies a blog post's Markdown source to the clipboard and a link to view the raw file. It fetches the `.md` file corresponding to the current page, handles the copy operation with loading and success/error states, and automatically resets the button text after 2 seconds.

explanations.11: Status is a type that can only be one of these four string values, representing the current state of the copy operation.
explanations.28: This constructs the URL to the Markdown file by taking the current page's URL, removing any trailing slash, and appending `.md` — so `/blog/my-post/` becomes `/blog/my-post.md`.
explanations.30: useCallback memoizes this function so it doesn't get recreated on every render, which matters because it's used as a dependency in useEffect below.
explanations.34: If the HTTP response indicates failure (status 4xx or 5xx), we throw an error to jump to the catch block rather than trying to process bad data.
explanations.36: navigator.clipboard.writeText is the browser API that puts text into the user's clipboard.
explanations.45: This early return prevents the timer from running when status is 'idle' or 'copying' — we only want to reset after showing success or error.
explanations.46: setTimeout returns a timer ID that we save so we can cancel it if the component unmounts or the status changes before 2 seconds pass.
explanations.47: The cleanup function returned from useEffect will cancel any pending timer when the component unmounts or when status changes, preventing memory leaks.
explanations.56: The button is disabled while copying is in progress so the user can't accidentally trigger multiple concurrent fetch requests.
explanations.58: This nested ternary shows different translated text depending on whether the copy succeeded, failed, or is still in the idle state.
